Talent Journey Ecosystem Architecture
The lifecycle flow is positioned inside an end-to-end business, application, data and governance architecture.
All architecture nodes open in pop-up · connected to Stage 1–10
Target Architecture
Connected Talent Journey from Job Seeker to Employee, Former Employee and Rehire
Every lifecycle event should create a controlled process status, a traceable owner, a reusable data record and a decision-ready insight. Talent Acquisition and Talent Development operate under one HC Development department.
Business firstProcess names remain business activities; applications are enablers.
One identityPerson ID links Candidate ID, Employee ID and portal identities.
Changeable blueprintPending decisions stay visible until approved by process owners.

Journey principleOne person can move across multiple roles and application records without losing lifecycle history.
System principleEach journey step has one primary business capability and one or more supporting systems.
Control principleEvery Hold, Pending and exception must have owner, reason, next action and target date.

HC Development — Integrated Department Operating Model
Talent Acquisition and Talent Development are consolidated into one department while retaining distinct professional functions, process ownership and KPI drill-down.
Recommended organization architecture
HC

HC Development Department

End-to-end stewardship of talent supply, selection, readiness, development and lifecycle intelligence.

Talent Acquisition & Fulfillment
  • Job Order validation and demand pipeline
  • Talent pool, sourcing and Job Matching
  • Tele Interview, assessment and internal selection
  • Replacement sourcing and candidate readiness
Talent Development & Learning
  • Learning-needs review and program assignment
  • Mandatory onboarding learning
  • Pre/post-test, completion and certificate
  • Skill readiness, coaching support and rehire development
Talent Analytics & EcosystemRecommended future function
  • Talent 360 and identity/data quality
  • Pipeline, skill and learning analytics
  • Dashboard governance and system roadmap
  • Readiness, rehire and replacement intelligence

Sales / AccountClient demand, candidate submission, deployment, extension and replacement initiation.
HC OperationalOffer handover, documents, contract, onboarding, employment and contract closure.
Managers / Client PICTechnical selection, performance feedback, coaching, readiness and approval.
Payroll / FinancePayroll readiness, billing, commercial control and restricted financial indicators.
IT / System OwnerApplication integration, identity, security, workflow, data platform and observability.

Governance & Integrity Rules
Rules applied across Process Master, connectors, dashboard and future systems.
Decision completeness

Every decision requires at least two branches, a next-action owner and a destination process.

Pending control

Hold, Pending and Dipertimbangkan require reason, owner, next action and follow-up date.

Identity continuity

Person ID remains the master identity; Candidate ID is linked to Employee ID after hiring.

Status separation

Job Order, Application, Tele Interview, Employment, Assignment, Learning and Contract statuses remain separate.

Core distinctions

Disarankan ≠ Ready for Client Submission; Ready for Matching ≠ Ready for Deployment; Deployed ≠ Billable.

Replacement traceability

Every case carries Original Job Order ID, previous talent reference and Replacement Case ID.

Restricted data

Psychometric details, salary, payroll nominal, billing rate, margin and sensitive feedback use role-based access.

End states

Every path ends in Active, Closed, Talent Pool, Former Employee or Archived; no process is allowed to hang.
